grading_method: Evaluator manually compared every requested material part of each answer with the fixed source-backed key and frozen summary; support labels did not determine grades. Key details not requested by question are not mandatory.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Shuffle Factory cards and randomly place number of players + 1 face-down on the board; return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: 'number of players + 1'; '11 marked territories'; 'one structure bonus tile'; 'The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.'
grades.reason: Factory selection/count/unseen return, 11 encounters, random face-up tile and lowest-mat starter resolved.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: Place each character at its home base; two workers, one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining the base; four mechs over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in matching boxes; four recruits on bottom-row circular spaces; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for first placement. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup pieces table and step 3: 'Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw'; 'Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives (two objective cards).'
grades.reason: Map and mat pieces, action-token starting location and correct assignment of starting values resolved.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action (or either or both); bottom-first is forbidden and you cannot return to the top action after bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before acting; exposed green-box benefits are optional and may be taken as much or as little as desired. Exact bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: 'must move the token'; 'First pay the full cost'; 'choose as much or as little ... benefit'; 'You may use top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost.'
grades.reason: Mandatory token move, optional actions/ordering, Rusviet exception, top gains below, exposed full costs/optional gains resolved.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: 'An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources'; 'Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control.'
grades.reason: Enemy worker control, owner-only persistent structure ability/Mill exception and remote resource spending resolved.

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: On a normal unupgraded Move, select up to two different units for one adjacent territory each; the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker's carried movement does not count as its own, so it may subsequently move itself, or may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech's later move. All units (characters, mechs, workers) carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry any number of your workers, never your character.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: 'two different units, one adjacent territory each'; 'Being carried does not count as the worker's own movement'; 'Only mechs may also carry ... your workers, never your character.'
grades.reason: Distinct-unit movement, transported worker own movement and all resource/mech worker transport restrictions resolved.

grades.question: What happens when a Speed-enabled mech enters enemy workers only, even at zero popularity; may its workers enter that territory by themselves?
grades.expected_answer: Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.observed_answer: The Speed-enabled mech stops and cannot move again that turn when it enters a territory occupied only by enemy workers; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero. Having zero popularity does not prevent the retreat. Your workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: 'Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops'; 'workers immediately retreat'; 'insufficient popularity does not prevent the retreat'; workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.reason: Enemy-worker-only stop, immediate home retreat/resources, popularity floor and independent worker-entry restriction resolved.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve all combat before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: 'Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order'; workers cannot independently move 'into or out of' territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
grades.reason: Combat after all movement/before bottom, attacker ordering and independent worker enter/leave prohibition resolved.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both are empty draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades; traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. You cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home. Built Monument adds one popularity to Bolster; built Armory adds one power to Trade.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster: '$1, gain two power OR one combat card'; 'If both are empty, draw none.' Trade: '$1'; resources on 'a controlled territory containing at least one worker'; 'cannot Trade ... if all your workers are at home.'
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production, then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades. Each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the current cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce steps: 'Pay every exposed Produce cost ... in full before production'; 'Take new workers from the Player Mat left to right'; 'You may decline some or all production'; new costs affect 'future Produce actions.'
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; put a chosen mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may still pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Upgrade — oil; Deploy — metal; placement on 'a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake'; 'Even after completing all ... you may still pay for that bottom action.'
grades.reason: Oil/metal resource costs, bracketed cube restrictions, worker/control/lake deployment and ability scope, completed-action payment resolved; no universal numerical cost was requested.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden, and only one structure total may occupy a territory. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A controlled Mill grants its bonus Produce territory and production; an enemy unit on its territory means you do not control it, so Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled. A Mine remains your personal tunnel for movement to and from it even while enemies occupy its territory, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions.
grades.reader_evidence: Build: 'controlled territory with your worker'; structures 'cannot be moved or destroyed'; Mill bonus applies 'only while controlled'; Mine allows movement 'even when enemy-controlled.'
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat; immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where you removed the recruit, not the one-time choice. When you or either immediate neighbor takes the matching bottom action, resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist: 'put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus'; ongoing bonus is the circle 'where you removed the recruit'; resolve 'active player first, then left, then right'; two-player opponent triggers once.
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Each combatant simultaneously and secretly selects dial power from 0 up to the smaller of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech (Rusviet People's Army permits one additional card total if any workers are present). If both players have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Both deduct selected dial power from their Power Tracks and discard every played card face-up; card values do not deduct track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–4: 'simultaneously and secretly choose'; 'Reveal simultaneously'; 'attacker wins ties'; both deduct dial power and discard cards face-up.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: Winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources; Nordic Seaworthy can instead retreat eligible units/carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, subject to Polania Camaraderie's stated exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 5–6 specify retreat of 'all characters, mechs and workers,' resources left, attacker popularity loss, defender none, and losing-player card condition.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains in the token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All gained resources, workers, mechs, and structures go to the encounter territory. Pay no additional normal action costs and gain no additional mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: 'after the whole Move action and all combats'; if entry is lost, 'the token stays'; gains go to 'the encounter territory'; 'no additional normal action costs' or mat benefits.
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Every player's character takes one Factory card on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory, after winning combat if necessary; each chooses one from the available cards and returns the rest. Each player may have at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); similar Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for a Speed-enabled character/mech, with normal restrictions (including Mine access and movement stops).
grades.reader_evidence: Factory: 'Every player's character, on its first finish of a Move action there'; 'one permanent card'; fifth action section; bottom action moves one unit up to two, or three with Speed.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: Reveal a completed objective only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action; you may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives: 'Only on your own turn'; 'meet all requirements at the moment of reveal'; put 'both objective cards on the bottom'; Saxony 'can score both.'
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars, Saxony unrestricted within six), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception; other players' stars do not block it. A placed star is permanent even if power or popularity later drops. The sixth star ends play immediately.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all goals; 'Other players’ stars never block a goal'; 'A placed star is permanent'; 'sixth star immediately ends play.'
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement part and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor recruit bonuses/stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player, left neighbor, right neighbor in order, checking for the sixth star each time; after an earlier player places the sixth star, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve.
grades.reader_evidence: Sixth-star sequence: collect 'primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing'; undo unresolved battle movement; neighbor sequence and stop condition stated.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At popularity 10, use the 7–12 tier: each of 5 stars adds $4 ($20 total); 4 normal territories plus Factory count as 4 + 3 = 7 scoring territories at $3 each ($21); 13 resources make 6 complete pairs at $2 each ($12). Thus those categories add $53 to held coins, before the selected structure bonus. The selected structure bonus is earned even if enemies control the territories containing your structures. Victory tiebreakers are workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring table gives 7–12 values ($4, $3, $2); Factory counts as 3; resource pairs round down; structure bonus earned despite enemy control; tiebreak order listed.
grades.reason: Tier-2 rates, Factory as three, floor pairs and $53, retained coins/structure eligibility and exact tiebreak order resolved.

grades.question: Is a home base a territory, may you enter one normally, and are expansion home bases active?
grades.expected_answer: Home base is not territory for any game effect; cannot normally move back in, build/deploy there. Starts and forced retreat exceptions; Crimea Wayfare explicit movement exception. Two unrepresented bases are expansion placeholders/inactive.
grades.observed_answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
grades.reader_evidence: Control section: 'A home base is not a territory'; default no entry/build/deploy, with listed exceptions; unmatched bases are inactive expansion placeholders.
grades.reason: Non-territory home base/default prohibitions, explicit exceptions and inactive expansion placeholders resolved.

grades.question: Which terrain produces each token, do Factory/lake produce, are workers resources, and what happens if resource supply runs out?
grades.expected_answer: Mountain metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village workers. Lake/Factory nothing. Workers not resources. Resource supply unlimited; use multipliers as necessary, no territory token/unit limit.
grades.observed_answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, villages workers; lakes and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce terrain table; 'workers are not resources'; 'Resource tokens have no supply limit: use multipliers if needed.'
grades.reason: All terrain outputs/no-output spaces, nonresource workers, unlimited resources and territory quantities resolved.

grades.question: May resources be picked up/dropped mid-movement, can mechs carry characters, and what does unlocked Speed change about tunnels and stops?
grades.expected_answer: All units may pick/drop any resources; mechs also own workers, never character. Speed adds one territory for character/mechs, including before/after tunnel jump which costs one move; may pick/drop mid-move. Entering enemy unit ends movement/cannot move again turn; character encounter also stops.
grades.observed_answer: Any unit may pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; mechs may also pick up/carry/drop your workers, but never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step and the extra step may be before or after it; mechs can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: all units carry resources; mechs carry workers but not character; Speed and tunnel step details and stop overrides stated.
grades.reason: All-unit resource pickup/drop, mech own-worker/no-character carriage, Speed/tunnel step and overriding stops resolved.

grades.question: Can workers capture a territory controlled only by an enemy structure, and are printed tunnels usable by all unit types?
grades.expected_answer: Yes any unit may enter structure-only territory and controls it; no combat from structure alone. All printed tunnel territories adjacent for Move by any unit; enemy Mine not a public tunnel.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: 'Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure'; 'All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.'
grades.reason: Any unit captures enemy structure-only territory, no structure combat, all-unit printed tunnels versus personal Mine resolved.

grades.question: If unable to afford any action after last using Move, must you pay a partial Produce cost or what turn is legal?
grades.expected_answer: Never partial payment; full cost required. Take a dead turn choosing another section with no actions, still moving token.
grades.observed_answer: You never pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action, a legal dead turn is to move the token to a different section and take neither action; thus after last using Move, choose a different section and skip both actions if necessary.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: 'If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn by moving the token to a different section and taking neither action. Never pay only part of a cost.'
grades.reason: Full payment required; legal dead turn shifts token and takes neither action resolved.

grades.question: What do Armory and Monument grant, when do those benefits trigger, and can an enemy occupant take them away?
grades.expected_answer: Armory adds 1 power when owner takes Trade, Monument adds 1 popularity when owner takes Bolster. Uncovered benefits apply future respective top actions, regardless territory control; opponent never gains them. Factory similar actions excluded.
grades.observed_answer: A built Armory grants one power on Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity on Bolster. These apply to the matching future action and the owner keeps the structure ability even without control, unless an uncontrolled Mill (the exception) is involved; an enemy occupant does not gain the building's ability.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster/Trade specify Monument and Armory bonuses; control section says you keep abilities without control and enemies do not gain them.
grades.reason: Trade Armory power/Bolster Monument popularity, future triggering and owner persistence versus enemy control resolved.

grades.question: How does each base faction Riverwalk differ, which units receive it, and does Nordic Swim give lake movement or help its mechs?
grades.expected_answer: Riverwalk only character/mechs: Saxony and Nordic forests/mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. Nordic faction Swim workers only across rivers to any land terrain, never lakes; no mech/character benefit.
grades.observed_answer: Riverwalk is for characters and mechs: Rusviet to farms/villages; Crimea to farms/tundra; Nordic to forests/mountains; Polania to villages/mountains; Saxony to forests/mountains. Nordic Swim instead lets workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help Nordic character/mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Faction ability table lists Riverwalk destinations for character/mechs; Nordic Swim says workers alone, not lakes, and not character/mechs.
grades.reason: All five Riverwalk terrain pairs/character-mech scope and worker-only Nordic river/not-lake Swim resolved.

grades.question: Which locations become adjacent under Saxony Underpass and Rusviet Township, and which units can use those shortcuts?
grades.expected_answer: Underpass controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent for character/mechs. Township controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mechs. Not workers; required ability unlocked via deploy.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use either shortcut.
grades.reader_evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township descriptions each specify 'character/mech Move actions.'
grades.reason: Saxony controlled mountains+tunnels and Rusviet controlled villages+Factory, character/mech-only adjacency resolved.

grades.question: When does Saxony Disarm apply, how often, and how does Nordic Artillery differ?
grades.expected_answer: Disarm before combat on printed tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses 2 power once per combat, not per unit. Artillery before any combat may pay 1 power to make opponent lose 2, once per combat. Track losses; attacker ability before defender.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine, making the opponent lose two power on the track, once per combat rather than per unit. Nordic Artillery instead lets you pay one power before combat to reduce the opponent's power by two, also once per combat rather than per unit.
grades.reader_evidence: Disarm and Artillery descriptions give timing, location/cost, effect, and once-per-combat frequency.
grades.reason: Saxony tunnel/Mine Disarm versus Nordic paid Artillery, timing/track reductions/once-per-combat resolved.

grades.question: With Rusviet People's Army, how many cards may two mechs and three workers play, and can workers alone fight?
grades.expected_answer: Three cards: one per mech plus one total for at least one worker. Need character/mech; workers alone cannot fight. Ability unlocked.
